name: Nanning Wuxu International Airport
before:
Guangxi's largest airport, 32 km south west of Nanning, and a designated gateway hub to ASEAN. It handled 13.5 million passengers in 2025, thirty third in China, though traffic was down about 4 per cent on the year.

Terminal 2 is the main building and a handsome one. Opened in September 2014, it covers 189,000 square metres across three floors with 32 air bridges and is built for 16 million passengers a year. Its design draws on the Han dynasty Phoenix Lantern found at Hepu in Guangxi.

There is a station on the Nanning to Pingxiang high speed railway at the airport itself, alongside two airport bus lines into the city, one to the Chaoyang Road ticket office near Nanning railway station and one to Wuxiang Square.

This is a joint civil and military field, so parts of the site are not public.

Growth here has been steep. The airport passed a million passengers in 2002, two million by 2006 and fifteen million by 2019.
after:
Guangxi's largest airport, 32 km south west of Nanning. It handled 13.5 million passengers in 2025, thirty third in China, though traffic was down about 4 per cent on the year.

Terminal 2 is the main building and a handsome one. It opened in September 2014, covers 189,000 square metres and was built for 16 million passengers a year, with a shape inspired by the phoenix.

The airport has its own railway station, called Wuxu Airport. Airport buses also run into the city.
